rules.rule_name: Session Existence Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that an active user session exists before allowing access to the main menu. If no session data is present, the user is redirected to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Session Validation
No session found

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the main menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: No session communication area exists (session length equals zero), indicating no prior authenticated session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the originating program to 'COSGN00C' and redirects the user to the Sign-On screen, denying access to the menu

rules.rule_name: Initial Menu Screen Display on First Visit
rules.rule_description: On the first visit to the menu within an active session, the system initializes the screen and displays the menu to the user without processing any input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Initial Menu Display
Initialize & Send Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and has navigated to the main menu for the first time
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects that the menu has not yet been entered (program re-entry flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-enterable, clears the menu screen output area to low values, populates the header information (title, transaction ID, program name, current date and time), builds up to 12 menu options, and sends the menu screen to the user

rules.rule_name: Menu Screen Input Capture on Returning Visit
rules.rule_description: On a returning visit to the menu screen, the system captures the user's input from the screen before processing any actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Menu Screen Input Capture
Receive User Input from Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and has previously been presented with the main menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits input from the menu screen (the program re-entry flag is already set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives and loads the user's screen input (including the selected option and the key pressed) into the input area for further processing

rules.rule_name: PF3 Key Navigation Back to Sign-On
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the menu screen, the system navigates the user back to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Navigation Key Handling
PF3 Pressed - Go Back

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' and transfers control to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Press Handling
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3, the system treats it as an invalid action and displays an error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Navigation Key Handling
Invalid Key Pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than the ENTER key or PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', populates the error message with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the menu screen with the error message shown

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Number Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that the option entered by the user is a numeric value, falls within the available menu option range, and is not zero.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Menu Option Input Validation
Validate Option Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed ENTER on the main menu screen and entered a value in the option field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the entered option after trimming trailing spaces and replacing remaining spaces with zeros
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the entered option is not numeric, OR is greater than the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), OR equals zero, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the message 'Please enter a valid option number...' and redisplays the menu screen; otherwise processing continues

rules.rule_name: Admin-Only Option Access Control
rules.rule_description: Enforces that menu options designated as Admin-Only are not accessible to regular users. Only administrators may select options flagged with user type 'A'.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:User Access Control Check
Check User Permission for Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option number and the option passes numeric and range validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The logged-in user is identified as a regular user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is true) AND the selected menu option is designated as Admin-Only (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the selected option equals 'A')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, clears the message area, populates the error message with 'No access - Admin Only option... ', and redisplays the menu screen; the user is not transferred to the selected program

rules.rule_name: Program Availability Verification for COPAUS0C
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system verifies that the program is installed and available in the environment.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Program Availability Check
Verify COPAUS0C is Installed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option that maps to the program 'COPAUS0C' and has the required access permissions
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the program 'COPAUS0C' is installed and available
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program is installed (response is NORMAL), the system sets the originating transaction ID and program name, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to 'COPAUS0C' with the session communication area; if the program is NOT installed, the system clears the message area, sets the error message color to RED, and displays the message 'This option [option name] is not installed...' then redisplays the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Coming Soon Option Handling
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder (dummy) program, the system informs the user that the feature is not yet available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Coming Soon Option Handling
Show Coming Soon Message in Green

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option with the required access permissions
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected option begins with 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters equal 'DUMMY')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the message color to GREEN, displays the message 'This option [option name] is coming soon...' and redisplays the menu screen without transferring the user to any program

rules.rule_name: Standard Program Navigation for Valid Options
rules.rule_description: For all valid, accessible, installed menu options that are not COPAUS0C or DUMMY programs, the system transfers control directly to the selected program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Menu Option Navigation
Transfer to Selected Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option, has the required access permissions, and the option is not mapped to 'COPAUS0C' or a 'DUMMY' program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the option maps to a standard installed program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the originating transaction ID to the current transaction ID, sets the originating program name to the current program name, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the program mapped to the selected option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME for the selected option) passing the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Return to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: Transfers the user to the Sign-On screen, defaulting to 'COSGN00C' if no specific destination program has been set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Return to Sign-On
Redirect to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen (either due to no session, PF3 press, or explicit redirect)
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either low-values or spaces (no specific target set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system defaults the destination program to 'COSGN00C' and transfers control to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Information Population
rules.rule_description: Each time the menu screen is displayed, the header section is refreshed with current application titles, transaction details, and the current date and time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Header Information Population
Populate Title, TransID, Program, Date, Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display or redisplay the main menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The header population routine is executed as part of the send menu screen process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time, populates the screen header with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current program name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

rules.rule_name: Menu Options List Construction
rules.rule_description: Builds the displayable menu option list by formatting each available option as a numbered entry and placing it in the corresponding screen field, supporting up to 12 options.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Menu Options Display Build
Build up to 12 menu option entries

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the main menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The menu options build routine is executed, iterating through all available options from 1 up to the total menu option count (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each option (1 through 12), the system formats the display text as '[option number]. [option name]' and places it into the corresponding screen output field (OPTN001O through OPTN012O respectively); any options beyond position 12 are ignored

rules.rule_name: Error Message Display on Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: Displays the appropriate error or informational message on the menu screen whenever a validation failure or access denial occurs, then redisplays the menu so the user can take corrective action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Error Message Display
Show Invalid Key Error / Show Invalid Option Error / Show Admin Only Access Denied / Show Program Not Installed Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: A validation failure, access denial, or informational condition has been detected during menu interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the menu screen after any of the following conditions: invalid key pressed, invalid option number entered, admin-only access denied, or program not installed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system moves the current value of WS-MESSAGE (containing the specific error or informational text) into the error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO) and sends the menu screen (MAP 'COMEN1A', MAPSET 'COMEN01') with ERASE, so the user sees the relevant message alongside the refreshed menu options

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD

    C[Set Sign-On Screen\nas the origin point]
    D[Redirect user to\nSign-On Screen\nto authenticate]
    E([End - Awaiting\nUser Authentication])
    F([Continue to\nMenu Processing])

rules.rule_name: Detect Missing User Session on Menu Entry
rules.rule_description: When the menu program starts, the system checks whether an active user session exists by verifying that session data was passed to the program. This is the entry gate that determines whether the user can proceed to the menu or must first authenticate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is there an active user session?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu program has just been invoked by the system
acceptance_criteria.When: No session data is present (the communication area length is zero, indicating no prior authenticated session exists)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines that the user does not have an active session and must be redirected to authenticate before accessing the menu

rules.rule_name: Record Sign-On Screen as the Session Origin Point
rules.rule_description: When no active session is detected, the system records the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the originating program before redirecting. This establishes the navigation context so the system knows where the unauthenticated request came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Sign-On Screen as the origin point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu program has been invoked and no active user session data is present
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the absence of a session and prepares to redirect the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records 'COSGN00C' (the Sign-On screen) as the originating program in the session navigation context (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), establishing the return point before the redirect is executed

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: When no active session exists, the system enforces authentication by transferring the user to the Sign-On screen. If no explicit target Sign-On program has been designated, the system defaults to the standard Sign-On program 'COSGN00C'. The user cannot access the menu until authentication is completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect user to Sign-On Screen to authenticate

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu program has been invoked, no active user session data is present, and the Sign-On screen has been recorded as the origin point
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the redirect to the Sign-On screen, and if no target Sign-On program is explicitly specified (target program is empty or blank), the system defaults the destination to 'COSGN00C'
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the Sign-On program ('COSGN00C'), the user is presented with the Sign-On screen to authenticate, and the menu remains inaccessible until a valid session is established

rules.rule_name: Detect First Visit to Main Menu
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is visiting the main menu for the first time within their current session, triggering the initial display sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Visit to Main Menu Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session with a valid communication area (session context exists)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks the session flag CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and finds it is NOT set to TRUE (indicating this is the first visit to the menu in this session)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds with the initial menu display sequence — marking the menu as visited, clearing the screen, and displaying the menu with all options and header information

rules.rule_name: Mark Menu as Visited for Subsequent Interactions
rules.rule_description: Once the first visit is detected, the session flag is updated so that any subsequent interaction with the menu screen is treated as a return visit, enabling input processing rather than re-initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Menu as Visited so next interaction is treated as a return visit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first visit to the main menu in the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The initial menu display sequence begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, so that the next time the user interacts with this screen, the system will process their input rather than re-displaying a fresh menu

rules.rule_name: Clear Menu Screen Before Display
rules.rule_description: Before populating and displaying the menu, all screen output fields are reset to blank (LOW-VALUES) to ensure no stale data from a previous session or screen is visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Menu Screen - Reset all screen fields to blank

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first visit to the main menu and has marked the session as visited
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for initial display
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields in the menu screen output area (COMEN1AO) are reset to LOW-VALUES (blank/empty), ensuring a clean slate before any data is populated

rules.rule_name: Populate Application Title on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The application's standard title lines are placed in the screen header area so the user can identify the application they are working within.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Application Title on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The header information is being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first title line (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the TITLE01O field of the menu screen, and the second title line (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the TITLE02O field of the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction ID and Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current transaction identifier and program name are displayed in the screen header, allowing users and support staff to identify the active transaction and program context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Transaction ID and Program Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.When: Transaction and program identification fields are being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the TRNNAMEO field of the menu screen, and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the PGMNAMEO field of the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Display Current Date in MM/DD/YY Format on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current system date is retrieved, formatted into MM/DD/YY format, and displayed in the screen header so the user can see the date of their current session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Current Date in MM/DD/YY format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The current date is being set on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date using FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, extracts the month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) into MM position, the day (WS-CURDATE-DAY) into DD position, and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3 and 4) into YY position, then places the combined MM/DD/YY formatted date into the CURDATEO field of the menu screen header

rules.rule_name: Display Current Time in HH:MM:SS Format on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current system time is retrieved, formatted into HH:MM:SS format, and displayed in the screen header so the user can see the time of their current session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Current Time in HH:MM:SS format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The current time is being set on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) into HH position, minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) into MM position, and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) into SS position from the current date/time data, then places the combined HH:MM:SS formatted time into the CURTIMEO field of the menu screen header

rules.rule_name: Format Each Menu Option as Number and Name
rules.rule_description: Each available menu option is formatted into a human-readable display line by combining the option number and option name, so users can clearly identify and select the desired function.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: For Each Available Menu Option - Combine Option Number and Option Name into a formatted display line

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is building the list of menu options to display
acceptance_criteria.When: Each menu option is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each option, the system concatenates the option number (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM), followed by a period and space ('. '), followed by the option name (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME), into a single formatted text line (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT) that will be shown to the user

rules.rule_name: Limit Menu Display to Maximum of 12 Options
rules.rule_description: The menu screen supports a maximum of 12 selectable options. The system iterates through all available options up to this limit, and any options beyond 12 are not displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More Options to Display? Up to 12

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is building the menu options list for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The loop iterates through available menu options using WS-IDX starting from 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The loop continues processing and placing options as long as WS-IDX does not exceed CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT (total available options); options are placed into screen slots OPTN001O through OPTN012O for option indices 1 through 12 respectively; any option index beyond 12 is ignored (CONTINUE); the loop stops when all available options have been processed

rules.rule_name: Place Formatted Option into Corresponding Screen Slot
rules.rule_description: Each formatted menu option line is placed into its designated screen display slot (1 through 12), ensuring options appear in the correct position on the menu screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Formatted Option into corresponding screen slot - Option 1 through Option 12

acceptance_criteria.Given: A menu option has been formatted as a display line (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The option is being assigned to its screen position based on its index (WS-IDX)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted option text is placed into the corresponding screen output field: index 1 → OPTN001O, index 2 → OPTN002O, index 3 → OPTN003O, index 4 → OPTN004O, index 5 → OPTN005O, index 6 → OPTN006O, index 7 → OPTN007O, index 8 → OPTN008O, index 9 → OPTN009O, index 10 → OPTN010O, index 11 → OPTN011O, index 12 → OPTN012O; any index value outside 1–12 results in no action (CONTINUE)

rules.rule_name: Send Completed Menu Screen to User
rules.rule_description: Once the header and all menu options have been populated, the completed menu screen is sent to the user's terminal, displaying all available options and header information, and awaiting user input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Completed Menu Screen with Header and All Options Visible

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu screen output area (COMEN1AO) has been fully populated with header information, all available menu options, and any applicable messages
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to present the menu to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) to the user's terminal using the fully populated output area (COMEN1AO), erasing any previous screen content, so the user sees a complete and current menu ready for input

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD

    G[Display Entered Option\nBack on Screen]

    A --> B
    B --> C

rules.rule_name: Capture User Input from Main Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the main menu screen, the system captures all input entered by the user, including the menu option number they have typed, making it available for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive User Input from Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and is viewing the main menu screen, and has pressed the ENTER key to submit their selection
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the submitted menu screen input from the user's terminal session
acceptance_criteria.Then: All user-entered data from the main menu screen, including the option number entered in the option input field, is captured and stored in the menu input data area (COMEN1AI) and is ready for further processing

rules.rule_name: Read Entered Option Number and Trim Trailing Spaces
rules.rule_description: After capturing the menu screen input, the system reads the raw option number entered by the user and removes any trailing spaces by scanning the option field from right to left to find the last meaningful (non-space) character, then extracts only the significant portion of the input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Entered Option Number from Input Field / Trim Trailing Spaces from Entered Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's menu screen input has been captured and the option input field (OPTIONI of COMEN1AI) contains the raw value entered by the user, which may include trailing spaces
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans the option input field from the rightmost character position backwards, decrementing one position at a time, until it finds a character that is not a space or reaches position 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the substring from position 1 up to and including the last non-space character position (WS-IDX), and stores this trimmed value into the working option field (WS-OPTION-X), effectively removing all trailing spaces from the entered option number

rules.rule_name: Replace Remaining Internal Spaces with Zeros
rules.rule_description: After trimming trailing spaces, any spaces that remain within the trimmed option value are replaced with zeros to normalize the input and ensure consistent numeric validation. This handles cases where the user may have entered spaces within or instead of a numeric option number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Replace Any Remaining Spaces with Zeros

acceptance_criteria.Given: The trimmed option value has been stored in the working option field (WS-OPTION-X) and may still contain internal or leading space characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system inspects the entire content of the working option field (WS-OPTION-X)
acceptance_criteria.Then: Every space character found anywhere within WS-OPTION-X is replaced with the character '0', so that a blank or partially blank entry is converted to a zero-padded numeric string, making the value ready for numeric validation

rules.rule_name: Store Normalized Option Number for Processing
rules.rule_description: The fully cleaned and normalized option number, with trailing spaces trimmed and internal spaces replaced by zeros, is stored into the designated option processing field so it can be used for all subsequent validation and navigation logic.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Cleaned Option Number for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The option input value has been trimmed of trailing spaces and all remaining spaces have been replaced with zeros, resulting in a normalized value in WS-OPTION-X
acceptance_criteria.When: The system moves the normalized option value from the working field (WS-OPTION-X) to the option processing field (WS-OPTION)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cleaned and normalized option number is stored in WS-OPTION and is available for all downstream business logic including numeric validation, range checking, access control, and program navigation

rules.rule_name: Display Entered Option Number Back on Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: After normalizing the user's entered option number, the system echoes the cleaned option value back to the menu screen output field, so the user can see exactly what option value the system has recorded and will process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Entered Option Back on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's entered option number has been cleaned and stored in the option processing field (WS-OPTION)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the menu screen for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The normalized option number from WS-OPTION is copied into the option output field (OPTIONO of COMEN1AO) on the menu screen, so that the value the system will act upon is visibly confirmed to the user on the screen

acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user pressed PF3 on the menu screen and the destination program has been set to 'COSGN00C', OR the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is empty or blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the return-to-sign-on navigation

rules.rule_name: Unrecognized Key Sets Invalid Key Error Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is neither the Enter key nor the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y' to signal that an invalid key was pressed

rules.rule_name: Unrecognized Key Loads Invalid Key Error Message

rules.rule_name: Menu Screen Redisplayed with Invalid Key Error Message

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Menu Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag is set to 'Y' and the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) has been loaded into the message field (WS-MESSAGE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the menu screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system refreshes the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name; populates all available menu options (up to 12, formatted as '[number]. rules.rule_name: Capture and Normalize Menu Option Input
rules.rule_description: When a user presses the Enter key on the menu screen, the system captures the option number entered, trims any trailing spaces from the right, and replaces any remaining internal spaces with zeros to produce a clean, normalized option value that is reflected back on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Option Number Entered by User / Clean Up Input Replace Spaces with Zeros

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has entered a value in the option input field (OPTIONI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key to submit their menu selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans the entered option from right to left to remove trailing spaces, extracts the meaningful portion of the input, replaces any remaining spaces within the value with zeros to normalize it, stores the cleaned value as the working option (WS-OPTION), and displays the normalized option value back in the option output field (OPTIONO) on the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Must Be a Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: The menu option entered by the user must be a numeric value. If the user enters any non-numeric characters, the system rejects the input, sets the error flag, displays an error message, and redisplays the menu screen for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the Entered Option Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key, and the input has been captured and normalized
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the normalized option value (WS-OPTION) contains only numeric digits
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value is NOT numeric, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: Even if the entered menu option is numeric, a value of zero is not a valid selection. The system must reject a zero value, set the error flag, display an error message, and redisplay the menu screen for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the Option Number Zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a numeric value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the normalized numeric option value (WS-OPTION) equals zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value equals zero (ZEROS), the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Must Be Within the Available Range of Options
rules.rule_description: The menu option entered by the user must not exceed the total number of menu options currently available. If the user enters a number greater than the maximum available options, the system rejects the input, sets the error flag, displays an error message, and redisplays the menu screen for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the Option Within Valid Range of Available Options?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a numeric, non-zero value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the normalized option value (WS-OPTION) against the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value is greater than the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

rules.rule_name: Display Validation Error and Redisplay Menu for Invalid Option Entry
rules.rule_description: When any of the menu option validations fail — the option is not numeric, equals zero, or exceeds the valid range — the system consolidates all three conditions into a single validation block, sets the error indicator, displays a unified error message, and refreshes the menu screen to allow the user to re-enter a valid option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message 'Please enter a valid option number...' / Redisplay Menu Screen for User to Correct Input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the menu screen and the system has captured and normalized the option input value (WS-OPTION)
acceptance_criteria.When: The option value (WS-OPTION) fails any one of the following conditions: (1) it is NOT numeric, OR (2) it exceeds the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), OR (3) it equals zero (ZEROS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', moves the error message 'Please enter a valid option number...' into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), and performs the SEND-MENU-SCREEN routine to redisplay the menu screen with the error message visible, allowing the user to correct and resubmit their option selection

rules.rule_name: Identify Regular User Attempting Admin-Only Menu Option
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the logged-in user is a Regular User AND the selected menu option is designated as Administrator-Only access. Both conditions must be true simultaneously to trigger an access denial.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the logged-in user a Regular User? / Is the selected option restricted to Admins Only?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application and has navigated to the Main Menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the logged-in user type is 'Regular User' (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE) AND the selected menu option's user-type designation is 'A' (Admin Only) as stored in CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the chosen option number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as an unauthorized access attempt and proceeds to deny access by activating the error flag (ERR-FLG-ON set to TRUE), clearing any prior message, populating the error message 'No access - Admin Only option...', and redisplaying the menu screen with the error message — the user remains on the menu screen and no navigation to the selected option occurs

rules.rule_name: Grant Unrestricted Menu Access to Administrator Users
rules.rule_description: Administrator users are not subject to the Admin-Only access restriction check. When the logged-in user is an Administrator, the system bypasses the access denial logic entirely and proceeds to process the selected menu option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Admin User → End: Access Granted - Proceed to Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application and has navigated to the Main Menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the logged-in user type is NOT a Regular User (i.e., the user is an Administrator, meaning CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not apply any Admin-Only restriction check regardless of the selected option's access designation, and proceeds directly to process and navigate to the selected menu option without displaying any access denial message

rules.rule_name: Grant Access When Selected Option Is Open to All Users
rules.rule_description: When a Regular User selects a menu option that is not restricted to Administrators only (i.e., the option is open to all user types), the system grants access and proceeds to process the selected option without any access denial.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Open to All Users → End: Access Granted - Proceed to Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application as a Regular User (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE) and has navigated to the Main Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the selected menu option's user-type designation (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the chosen option) is NOT equal to 'A' (i.e., the option is not Admin-Only)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not apply any access restriction, no error flag is set, no access denial message is displayed, and the system proceeds to process and navigate to the selected menu option

rules.rule_name: Set Access Denied Error State for Unauthorized Menu Selection
rules.rule_description: When a Regular User attempts to access an Admin-Only menu option, the system activates the error state flag to signal that an access violation has occurred, preventing any further processing of the selected option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Access Denied: Set Error Flag ON

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the logged-in user is a Regular User AND the selected menu option is designated as Admin-Only
acceptance_criteria.When: The access control check confirms both conditions are simultaneously true (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE AND CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the selected option equals 'A')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON (ERR-FLG-ON set to TRUE), which blocks all subsequent option processing logic from executing, ensuring the user cannot be transferred to the restricted program

rules.rule_name: Display Access Denied Error Message for Admin-Only Option
rules.rule_description: When access is denied due to a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option, the system clears any prior message and populates a specific access denial message to inform the user of the restriction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Error Message: 'No access - Admin Only option...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed that the logged-in user is a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option, and the error flag has been set to ON
acceptance_criteria.When: The access denial processing is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system first clears the message area (WS-MESSAGE is set to SPACES) and then populates it with the exact message: 'No access - Admin Only option...' to be displayed to the user on the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Menu Screen After Access Denial
rules.rule_description: After denying access to an Admin-Only option for a Regular User, the system redisplays the Main Menu screen with the access denial error message, keeping the user on the menu so they can select a permitted option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Menu Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to ON and populated the error message 'No access - Admin Only option...' due to a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option
acceptance_criteria.When: The SEND-MENU-SCREEN process is invoked, which populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name, builds all available menu options (up to 12) formatted as '[number]. [option name]', and moves the error message to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Main Menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) is refreshed and redisplayed to the user with the access denial message 'No access - Admin Only option...' visible in the error message area, the user remains on the menu screen, and no transfer to any other program occurs

rules.rule_name: Identify COPAUS0C as a Special Program Requiring Availability Verification
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to the COPAUS0C program, the system must treat it differently from other menu options by first verifying its availability before allowing navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Selected Menu Option COPAUS0C

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a menu option on the Main Menu screen and the option has been validated as a valid numeric option within range with no access restriction errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected menu option is exactly 'COPAUS0C'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must perform a program availability check on COPAUS0C before any navigation is attempted, distinguishing this option from standard menu options that navigate directly without a prior availability check

rules.rule_name: Verify COPAUS0C Program is Installed and Available Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring the user to the COPAUS0C program, the system must confirm that the program is physically installed and available in the application environment to prevent navigation failures.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Check if Program COPAUS0C is Available in the System

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected the menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C' and no validation or authorization errors exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs an inquiry on the program 'COPAUS0C' to determine its installation status
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system evaluates the response of the inquiry: if the response indicates the program is available (normal response), the system proceeds with navigation; if the response indicates the program is not available (any non-normal response), the system blocks navigation and triggers an error notification

rules.rule_name: Pass Session Context Information When Navigating to COPAUS0C
rules.rule_description: When the COPAUS0C program is confirmed as installed, the system must record the originating transaction and program details in the session context before transferring control, ensuring the destination program knows the navigation origin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass Session Information to Target Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the menu option mapped to 'COPAUS0C' and the program availability inquiry has returned a normal (successful) response confirming the program is installed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) record the current transaction ID into the session field 'From Transaction ID', (2) record the current program name into the session field 'From Program', (3) reset the program context value to zero, and (4) pass the full session communication area to the target program COPAUS0C

rules.rule_name: Navigate User to COPAUS0C Program When Available
rules.rule_description: Once session context is set and COPAUS0C is confirmed as installed, the system transfers full control to the COPAUS0C program, ending the current menu session and handing off to the target program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to COPAUS0C Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The session context fields (From Transaction ID, From Program, Program Context) have been populated and the COPAUS0C program has been confirmed as installed and available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control to program COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers complete control to the COPAUS0C program, passing the full session communication area, and the menu program relinquishes control — the user is now operating within the COPAUS0C program

rules.rule_name: Display Red Error Message When COPAUS0C Program is Not Installed
rules.rule_description: If the COPAUS0C program is found to be unavailable or not installed, the system must inform the user with a clearly visible red-colored error message that includes the specific option name, preventing any navigation attempt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message in Red: 'This option is not installed...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the menu option mapped to 'COPAUS0C' and the program availability inquiry has returned a non-normal response indicating the program is not installed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that COPAUS0C is not available in the environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) clear the current message area, (2) set the error message display color to RED, and (3) construct and display the message: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (trimmed at double-space boundary), so the user clearly understands the selected feature is unavailable

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Menu Screen After Program Not Installed Error
rules.rule_description: After displaying the 'not installed' error message, the system must refresh and redisplay the full menu screen so the user can review the error and select a different valid option without losing their session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Menu Screen for User to Select Another Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the COPAUS0C program is not installed and has constructed the red error message 'This option [option name] is not installed...'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the error message construction and no navigation has occurred
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must redisplay the full menu screen including: (1) refreshed header with current date, time, transaction ID and program name, (2) all available menu options formatted as '[number]. [option name]', and (3) the red error message visible in the error message area — allowing the user to select a different menu option

rules.rule_name: Identify Coming Soon Menu Option
rules.rule_description: Determine whether the selected menu option is mapped to a placeholder program, indicating the feature is not yet available for use.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does the Selected Option Map to a DUMMY Program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a menu option and the system is evaluating which program to invoke
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected menu option begins with the characters 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters of the program name equal 'DUMMY')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the selected option as a placeholder 'coming soon' feature and does NOT transfer control to any program; instead it proceeds to display a coming soon notification to the user

rules.rule_name: Clear Existing Message Before Coming Soon Notification
rules.rule_description: Before building and displaying the coming soon notification, any previously displayed message in the message area must be cleared to ensure a clean, accurate message is shown to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Any Existing Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has identified that the selected menu option maps to a DUMMY placeholder program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to build the coming soon notification message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message area (sets it to spaces/blank) so that no residual or prior message text remains before the new coming soon message is constructed

rules.rule_name: Set Coming Soon Message Display Color to Green
rules.rule_description: Coming soon notifications must be visually distinguished from error messages by displaying them in green color, signaling to the user that this is an informational notice rather than an error or warning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Message Color to Green

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has identified that the selected menu option maps to a DUMMY placeholder program and the message area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing to display the coming soon notification on the menu screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message display color attribute to GREEN, so the coming soon message is rendered in green on the screen, distinguishing it from error messages which appear in red

rules.rule_name: Build Coming Soon Message with Option Name
rules.rule_description: The coming soon notification message must be dynamically constructed by combining the literal text 'This option', the name of the selected menu option, and the phrase 'is coming soon ...' to provide a clear, context-specific message to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Build Coming Soon Message Combining Option Name with 'is coming soon ...' text

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has identified the selected option as a DUMMY placeholder, cleared the message area, and set the display color to green
acceptance_criteria.When: The system builds the coming soon notification message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system constructs the message by concatenating: the literal text 'This option ', followed by the name of the selected menu option (trimmed at the first space), followed by the literal text 'is coming soon ...', and stores this combined text into the message field to be displayed on the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Display Menu Screen with Coming Soon Notification
rules.rule_description: After building the coming soon notification, the system must redisplay the menu screen with the green coming soon message visible to the user, keeping the user on the menu so they can select a different available option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Menu Screen with Green Coming Soon Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The coming soon message has been built and the message color has been set to green
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes processing for a DUMMY placeholder menu option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system refreshes and sends the menu screen to the user with the header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name), all available menu options displayed, and the green coming soon message shown in the error message area — the user remains on the menu screen and is not transferred to any other program

rules.rule_name: Determine Program Navigation Path Based on Selected Menu Option
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a valid menu option with granted access, the system determines the appropriate navigation path by evaluating the program name associated with the selected option — routing to a special availability-checked program, a placeholder, or a standard program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which Program Type is Selected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option number and access has been granted (option is numeric, within range, not zero, and not an Admin-Only option for a regular user)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the program name mapped to the selected menu option
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program name is exactly 'COPAUS0C', the system follows the special availability-check path; if the first 5 characters of the program name are 'DUMMY', the system follows the coming-soon placeholder path; for all other program names, the system follows the standard program transfer path

rules.rule_name: Verify Availability of COPAUS0C Program Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system verifies that the program is currently installed and available in the environment to prevent navigation to a non-existent program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Program Available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is 'COPAUS0C'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the program 'COPAUS0C' is installed and available
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program is available, the system proceeds to record origin details and transfer control to COPAUS0C; if the program is not available, the system displays an error message and returns the user to the menu for correction

rules.rule_name: Record Origin Transaction ID Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system records the current transaction identifier as the originating transaction so the target program can identify where the navigation originated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction ID as Origin Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C' and the program has been confirmed as available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the origin transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

rules.rule_name: Record Origin Program Name Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system records the current program name as the originating program so the target program can identify the source of navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name as Origin Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C', the program is confirmed available, and the origin transaction ID has been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the origin program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system resets the program context indicator to zero, signaling to the target program that it is being entered fresh from the menu rather than from a mid-flow return.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Program Context to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C', the program is confirmed available, and both origin transaction ID and origin program name have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes preparation to transfer control to COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is set to zero (ZEROS) in the session communication area, indicating a fresh entry into the target program

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to COPAUS0C Program with Session Data
rules.rule_description: After confirming availability and recording origin details, the system transfers full control to the COPAUS0C program, passing the complete session communication area so the target program has all necessary context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to COPAUS0C Program with Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program 'COPAUS0C' is confirmed available, and the session communication area has been updated with the origin transaction ID, origin program name, and a reset program context of zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the program 'COPAUS0C' and the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the target program; the target program receives control with complete session information

rules.rule_name: Display Program Not Available Error When COPAUS0C Is Not Installed
rules.rule_description: When the user selects the menu option associated with COPAUS0C but the program is not installed in the environment, the system informs the user with a clearly highlighted error message and returns them to the menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Program Not Available Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that the program 'COPAUS0C' is not installed or not available
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the error message color to RED, and displays the message: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option, delimited by two spaces); the user is returned to the menu screen for correction

rules.rule_name: Display Coming Soon Message for Placeholder Menu Options
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder program (not yet implemented), the system informs the user that the feature is planned but not yet available, without navigating away from the menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Coming Soon Message in Green

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name begins with 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters equal 'DUMMY')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the program type for the selected option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the message color to GREEN, and displays the message: 'This option [option name] is coming soon ...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option, delimited by a single space); the user remains on the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Record Origin Transaction ID Before Transferring to Standard Program

rules.rule_name: Record Origin Program Name Before Transferring to Standard Program

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name as Origin Program

acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the selected standard program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the origin program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context Before Transferring to Standard Program
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to any standard program, the system resets the program context indicator to zero, signaling to the target program that it is being entered fresh from the menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Program Context to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is not 'COPAUS0C' and does not begin with 'DUMMY', and both origin transaction ID and origin program name have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes preparation to transfer control to the selected standard program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is set to zero (ZEROS) in the session communication area, indicating a fresh entry into the target program

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Selected Standard Program with Session Data
rules.rule_description: After recording origin details and resetting program context, the system transfers full control to the user's selected standard program, passing the complete session communication area so the target program has all necessary context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Selected Program with Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to a standard program (not 'COPAUS0C' and not beginning with 'DUMMY'), and the session communication area has been updated with the origin transaction ID, origin program name, and a reset program context of zero

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the absence of an active session upon screen entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the originating program reference to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On program) and immediately redirects the user to the Sign-On screen, preventing any access to the menu without authentication

rules.rule_name: Return to Sign-On Screen When User Presses PF3
rules.rule_description: When an authenticated user on the main menu screen explicitly presses PF3, the system treats this as a deliberate request to go back or log out, and routes the user back to the Sign-On screen.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and initiates the return-to-sign-on process, transferring the user back to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen When Not Explicitly Set
rules.rule_description: Before transferring the user to the Sign-On screen, the system verifies that a destination program has been explicitly set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults it to the Sign-On program to ensure the user always lands on a valid screen.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The return-to-sign-on process has been triggered either due to no active session or PF3 key press

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system automatically sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) as the default, ensuring no transfer occurs to an undefined or blank destination

rules.rule_name: Transfer User Control to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A menu option has been formatted and the current index position is 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted text to the appropriate screen display field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted option text (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT) is placed into screen display field OPTN010O, making it visible to the user in menu position 10

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Placement at Screen Position 11
rules.rule_description: The formatted menu option text for the eleventh menu item is assigned to the eleventh designated display slot on the menu screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Text in Menu Position 11

acceptance_criteria.Given: A menu option has been formatted and the current index position is 11
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted text to the appropriate screen display field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted option text (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT) is placed into screen display field OPTN011O, making it visible to the user in menu position 11

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Placement at Screen Position 12
rules.rule_description: The formatted menu option text for the twelfth menu item is assigned to the twelfth designated display slot on the menu screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Text in Menu Position 12

acceptance_criteria.Given: A menu option has been formatted and the current index position is 12
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted text to the appropriate screen display field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted option text (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT) is placed into screen display field OPTN012O, making it visible to the user in menu position 12

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Beyond Maximum Supported Display Range is Skipped
rules.rule_description: The menu screen supports a maximum of 12 visible option slots. If the total number of configured menu options exceeds 12, any option beyond position 12 is silently skipped and not displayed on the screen. This enforces the maximum display capacity of the menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip - Position Beyond Supported Range

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is building the menu option list and the current index position is greater than 12
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which screen position to assign the formatted option text to
acceptance_criteria.Then: No screen display field is updated for that option; the option is silently skipped (CONTINUE), the loop advances to the next index, and the menu screen displays a maximum of 12 options regardless of how many options are configured

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Index Increment for Next Iteration
rules.rule_description: After each menu option has been formatted and placed (or skipped), the system advances the current index by 1 to process the next available menu option in sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to Next Option Index

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed processing the current menu option at the current index (either placed on screen or skipped)
acceptance_criteria.When: The current iteration of the menu build loop concludes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current index (WS-IDX) is incremented by 1 and the loop condition is re-evaluated to determine whether additional menu options remain to be processed
