rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Press Error Handling
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the menu screen, the system sets an error condition and loads the standard invalid key error message to be displayed on the menu screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invalid Key Pressed / Set Error Flag ON / Load Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session, and the menu screen has been previously displayed awaiting user input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than the ENTER key or PF3 function key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) is set to 'Y' (ON), the system standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is loaded into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), and the menu screen is redisplayed with the error message so the user can correct their action

rules.rule_name: Invalid Menu Option Number Validation
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a menu option that is non-numeric, equals zero, or exceeds the total number of available menu options, the system rejects the input and prompts the user to enter a valid option number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invalid Option Number Not Numeric / Zero / Out of Range / Set Error Flag ON / Load Message: 'Please enter a valid option number...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session and presses the ENTER key to submit a menu option selection
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered option value (WS-OPTION) is not a numeric value, OR the entered option value equals zero, OR the entered option value is greater than the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) is set to 'Y' (ON), the message 'Please enter a valid option number...' is loaded into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), and the menu screen is redisplayed with the error message so the user can enter a valid option

rules.rule_name: Admin-Only Option Access Denial for Regular Users
rules.rule_description: When a regular (non-administrator) user selects a menu option that is designated as Administrator-only, the system denies access and displays an appropriate message, preventing the user from proceeding to that function.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Access Denied Admin Only Option Selected by Regular User / Set Error Flag ON / Load Message: 'No access - Admin Only option...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen, the user's account type is identified as a regular user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is true), and the user has entered a valid numeric option number within range
acceptance_criteria.When: The selected menu option's user-type designation (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the selected option) is equal to 'A' (Admin Only)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag (ERR-FLG-ON) is set to TRUE, the message field (WS-MESSAGE) is first cleared to spaces and then loaded with 'No access - Admin Only option...', and the menu screen is redisplayed with the access denial message so the user can select a permitted option

rules.rule_name: Unavailable Program Error Notification
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the specific menu option mapped to program COPAUS0C and that program is not currently installed or available in the system, the system displays an error message in red color indicating the option is unavailable.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Program Not Available / Not Installed / Load Message in RED: 'This option name is not installed...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen, has entered a valid option number with no prior errors, and the selected option is mapped to the program COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks program availability and the program COPAUS0C is determined to be not installed or not available (EIBRESP is not NORMAL)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message field (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces, the error message color attribute (ERRMSGC of COMEN1AO) is set to RED (DFHRED), and a message is constructed and loaded into WS-MESSAGE in the format: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option), delimited at double-space; the menu screen is then redisplayed with this red error message

rules.rule_name: Coming Soon Feature Notification
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder program (not yet implemented), the system informs the user that the feature is planned but not yet available, displaying the message in green color.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Coming Soon Feature Not Yet Available / Load Message in GREEN: 'This option name is coming soon...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen, has entered a valid option number with no prior errors, and the selected option is not mapped to program COPAUS0C
acceptance_criteria.When: The first 5 characters of the program name associated with the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME for the selected option) equal 'DUMMY'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message field (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces, the error message color attribute (ERRMSGC of COMEN1AO) is set to GREEN (DFHGREEN), and a message is constructed and loaded into WS-MESSAGE in the format: 'This option [option name] is coming soon...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option), delimited at first space; the menu screen is then redisplayed with this green informational message

rules.rule_name: Error Message Transfer to Screen Display Field
rules.rule_description: Before redisplaying the menu screen, any error or informational message that has been loaded into the working storage message field is transferred to the corresponding screen output field so it becomes visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Error Message to Screen Error Message Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected, an appropriate message has been loaded into the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE), and the system is preparing to redisplay the menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The send menu screen process is initiated (SEND-MENU-SCREEN is performed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) is moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO), making the message available for display to the user on the menu screen

rules.rule_name: Menu Screen Redisplay After Error
rules.rule_description: After any error condition is detected and the error message is prepared, the menu screen is refreshed and sent back to the user with updated header information, all menu options, and the error message displayed, allowing the user to review and correct their input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Menu Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected, the appropriate error message has been moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO), the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID and program name, and all available menu options (up to 12) have been formatted and placed in their respective screen option fields (OPTN001O through OPTN012O)
acceptance_criteria.When: The menu screen send operation is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) is sent to the user's terminal using the populated output map (COMEN1AO) with the ERASE option, displaying the refreshed menu with all options and the error message visible, so the user can review the error and re-enter their selection

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the main menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No session communication area exists (session length equals zero), indicating no prior authenticated session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the originating program to 'COSGN00C' and redirects the user to the Sign-On screen, denying access to the menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Existence Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that an active user session exists before allowing access to the main menu. If no session data is present, the user is redirected to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and has navigated to the main menu for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects that the menu has not yet been entered (program re-entry flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-enterable, clears the menu screen output area to low values, populates the header information (title, transaction ID, program name, current date and time), builds up to 12 menu options, and sends the menu screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Menu Screen Display on First Visit
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first visit to the menu within an active session, the system initializes the screen and displays the menu to the user without processing any input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and has previously been presented with the main menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits input from the menu screen (the program re-entry flag is already set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives and loads the user's screen input (including the selected option and the key pressed) into the input area for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Screen Input Capture on Returning Visit
all_rules.Rule_Description: On a returning visit to the menu screen, the system captures the user's input from the screen before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' and transfers control to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Key Navigation Back to Sign-On
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the menu screen, the system navigates the user back to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than the ENTER key or PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', populates the error message with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the menu screen with the error message shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Press Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3, the system treats it as an invalid action and displays an error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed ENTER on the main menu screen and entered a value in the option field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the entered option after trimming trailing spaces and replacing remaining spaces with zeros
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered option is not numeric, OR is greater than the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), OR equals zero, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the message 'Please enter a valid option number...' and redisplays the menu screen; otherwise processing continues

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Option Number Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the option entered by the user is a numeric value, falls within the available menu option range, and is not zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option number and the option passes numeric and range validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The logged-in user is identified as a regular user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is true) AND the selected menu option is designated as Admin-Only (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the selected option equals 'A')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, clears the message area, populates the error message with 'No access - Admin Only option... ', and redisplays the menu screen; the user is not transferred to the selected program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Admin-Only Option Access Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that menu options designated as Admin-Only are not accessible to regular users. Only administrators may select options flagged with user type 'A'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option that maps to the program 'COPAUS0C' and has the required access permissions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the program 'COPAUS0C' is installed and available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the program is installed (response is NORMAL), the system sets the originating transaction ID and program name, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to 'COPAUS0C' with the session communication area; if the program is NOT installed, the system clears the message area, sets the error message color to RED, and displays the message 'This option [option name] is not installed...' then redisplays the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Availability Verification for COPAUS0C
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system verifies that the program is installed and available in the environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option with the required access permissions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected option begins with 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters equal 'DUMMY')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the message color to GREEN, displays the message 'This option [option name] is coming soon...' and redisplays the menu screen without transferring the user to any program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Coming Soon Option Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder (dummy) program, the system informs the user that the feature is not yet available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option, has the required access permissions, and the option is not mapped to 'COPAUS0C' or a 'DUMMY' program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the option maps to a standard installed program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the originating transaction ID to the current transaction ID, sets the originating program name to the current program name, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the program mapped to the selected option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME for the selected option) passing the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Standard Program Navigation for Valid Options
all_rules.Rule_Description: For all valid, accessible, installed menu options that are not COPAUS0C or DUMMY programs, the system transfers control directly to the selected program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen (either due to no session, PF3 press, or explicit redirect)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either low-values or spaces (no specific target set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system defaults the destination program to 'COSGN00C' and transfers control to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Transfers the user to the Sign-On screen, defaulting to 'COSGN00C' if no specific destination program has been set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display or redisplay the main menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The header population routine is executed as part of the send menu screen process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time, populates the screen header with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current program name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Information Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time the menu screen is displayed, the header section is refreshed with current application titles, transaction details, and the current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the main menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The menu options build routine is executed, iterating through all available options from 1 up to the total menu option count (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each option (1 through 12), the system formats the display text as '[option number]. [option name]' and places it into the corresponding screen output field (OPTN001O through OPTN012O respectively); any options beyond position 12 are ignored

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Options List Construction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Builds the displayable menu option list by formatting each available option as a numbered entry and placing it in the corresponding screen field, supporting up to 12 options.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validation failure, access denial, or informational condition has been detected during menu interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the menu screen after any of the following conditions: invalid key pressed, invalid option number entered, admin-only access denied, or program not installed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the current value of WS-MESSAGE (containing the specific error or informational text) into the error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO) and sends the menu screen (MAP 'COMEN1A', MAPSET 'COMEN01') with ERASE, so the user sees the relevant message alongside the refreshed menu options

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Display on Menu Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Displays the appropriate error or informational message on the menu screen whenever a validation failure or access denial occurs, then redisplays the menu so the user can take corrective action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu program has just been invoked by the system
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No session data is present (the communication area length is zero, indicating no prior authenticated session exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines that the user does not have an active session and must be redirected to authenticate before accessing the menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing User Session on Menu Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the menu program starts, the system checks whether an active user session exists by verifying that session data was passed to the program. This is the entry gate that determines whether the user can proceed to the menu or must first authenticate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu program has been invoked and no active user session data is present
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the absence of a session and prepares to redirect the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records 'COSGN00C' (the Sign-On screen) as the originating program in the session navigation context (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), establishing the return point before the redirect is executed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Sign-On Screen as the Session Origin Point
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session is detected, the system records the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the originating program before redirecting. This establishes the navigation context so the system knows where the unauthenticated request came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu program has been invoked, no active user session data is present, and the Sign-On screen has been recorded as the origin point
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the redirect to the Sign-On screen, and if no target Sign-On program is explicitly specified (target program is empty or blank), the system defaults the destination to 'COSGN00C'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the Sign-On program ('COSGN00C'), the user is presented with the Sign-On screen to authenticate, and the menu remains inaccessible until a valid session is established

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session exists, the system enforces authentication by transferring the user to the Sign-On screen. If no explicit target Sign-On program has been designated, the system defaults to the standard Sign-On program 'COSGN00C'. The user cannot access the menu until authentication is completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session with a valid communication area (session context exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks the session flag CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and finds it is NOT set to TRUE (indicating this is the first visit to the menu in this session)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds with the initial menu display sequence — marking the menu as visited, clearing the screen, and displaying the menu with all options and header information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First Visit to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is visiting the main menu for the first time within their current session, triggering the initial display sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first visit to the main menu in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initial menu display sequence begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, so that the next time the user interacts with this screen, the system will process their input rather than re-displaying a fresh menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Menu as Visited for Subsequent Interactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the first visit is detected, the session flag is updated so that any subsequent interaction with the menu screen is treated as a return visit, enabling input processing rather than re-initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first visit to the main menu and has marked the session as visited
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for initial display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields in the menu screen output area (COMEN1AO) are reset to LOW-VALUES (blank/empty), ensuring a clean slate before any data is populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Menu Screen Before Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating and displaying the menu, all screen output fields are reset to blank (LOW-VALUES) to ensure no stale data from a previous session or screen is visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The header information is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first title line (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the TITLE01O field of the menu screen, and the second title line (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the TITLE02O field of the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The application's standard title lines are placed in the screen header area so the user can identify the application they are working within.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Transaction and program identification fields are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the TRNNAMEO field of the menu screen, and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the PGMNAMEO field of the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID and Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current transaction identifier and program name are displayed in the screen header, allowing users and support staff to identify the active transaction and program context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current date is being set on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date using FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, extracts the month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) into MM position, the day (WS-CURDATE-DAY) into DD position, and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3 and 4) into YY position, then places the combined MM/DD/YY formatted date into the CURDATEO field of the menu screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Date in MM/DD/YY Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date is retrieved, formatted into MM/DD/YY format, and displayed in the screen header so the user can see the date of their current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current time is being set on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) into HH position, minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) into MM position, and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) into SS position from the current date/time data, then places the combined HH:MM:SS formatted time into the CURTIMEO field of the menu screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Time in HH:MM:SS Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time is retrieved, formatted into HH:MM:SS format, and displayed in the screen header so the user can see the time of their current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is building the list of menu options to display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each menu option is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each option, the system concatenates the option number (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM), followed by a period and space ('. '), followed by the option name (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME), into a single formatted text line (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT) that will be shown to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Each Menu Option as Number and Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each available menu option is formatted into a human-readable display line by combining the option number and option name, so users can clearly identify and select the desired function.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is building the menu options list for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The loop iterates through available menu options using WS-IDX starting from 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The loop continues processing and placing options as long as WS-IDX does not exceed CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT (total available options); options are placed into screen slots OPTN001O through OPTN012O for option indices 1 through 12 respectively; any option index beyond 12 is ignored (CONTINUE); the loop stops when all available options have been processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Limit Menu Display to Maximum of 12 Options
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu screen supports a maximum of 12 selectable options. The system iterates through all available options up to this limit, and any options beyond 12 are not displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A menu option has been formatted as a display line (WS-MENU-OPT-TXT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The option is being assigned to its screen position based on its index (WS-IDX)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted option text is placed into the corresponding screen output field: index 1 → OPTN001O, index 2 → OPTN002O, index 3 → OPTN003O, index 4 → OPTN004O, index 5 → OPTN005O, index 6 → OPTN006O, index 7 → OPTN007O, index 8 → OPTN008O, index 9 → OPTN009O, index 10 → OPTN010O, index 11 → OPTN011O, index 12 → OPTN012O; any index value outside 1–12 results in no action (CONTINUE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Formatted Option into Corresponding Screen Slot
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each formatted menu option line is placed into its designated screen display slot (1 through 12), ensuring options appear in the correct position on the menu screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen output area (COMEN1AO) has been fully populated with header information, all available menu options, and any applicable messages
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to present the menu to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) to the user's terminal using the fully populated output area (COMEN1AO), erasing any previous screen content, so the user sees a complete and current menu ready for input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Completed Menu Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the header and all menu options have been populated, the completed menu screen is sent to the user's terminal, displaying all available options and header information, and awaiting user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and is viewing the main menu screen, and has pressed the ENTER key to submit their selection
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the submitted menu screen input from the user's terminal session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All user-entered data from the main menu screen, including the option number entered in the option input field, is captured and stored in the menu input data area (COMEN1AI) and is ready for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User Input from Main Menu Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the main menu screen, the system captures all input entered by the user, including the menu option number they have typed, making it available for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's menu screen input has been captured and the option input field (OPTIONI of COMEN1AI) contains the raw value entered by the user, which may include trailing spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans the option input field from the rightmost character position backwards, decrementing one position at a time, until it finds a character that is not a space or reaches position 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the substring from position 1 up to and including the last non-space character position (WS-IDX), and stores this trimmed value into the working option field (WS-OPTION-X), effectively removing all trailing spaces from the entered option number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Entered Option Number and Trim Trailing Spaces
all_rules.Rule_Description: After capturing the menu screen input, the system reads the raw option number entered by the user and removes any trailing spaces by scanning the option field from right to left to find the last meaningful (non-space) character, then extracts only the significant portion of the input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The trimmed option value has been stored in the working option field (WS-OPTION-X) and may still contain internal or leading space characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects the entire content of the working option field (WS-OPTION-X)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every space character found anywhere within WS-OPTION-X is replaced with the character '0', so that a blank or partially blank entry is converted to a zero-padded numeric string, making the value ready for numeric validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Replace Remaining Internal Spaces with Zeros
all_rules.Rule_Description: After trimming trailing spaces, any spaces that remain within the trimmed option value are replaced with zeros to normalize the input and ensure consistent numeric validation. This handles cases where the user may have entered spaces within or instead of a numeric option number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The option input value has been trimmed of trailing spaces and all remaining spaces have been replaced with zeros, resulting in a normalized value in WS-OPTION-X
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system moves the normalized option value from the working field (WS-OPTION-X) to the option processing field (WS-OPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cleaned and normalized option number is stored in WS-OPTION and is available for all downstream business logic including numeric validation, range checking, access control, and program navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Normalized Option Number for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully cleaned and normalized option number, with trailing spaces trimmed and internal spaces replaced by zeros, is stored into the designated option processing field so it can be used for all subsequent validation and navigation logic.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's entered option number has been cleaned and stored in the option processing field (WS-OPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the menu screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The normalized option number from WS-OPTION is copied into the option output field (OPTIONO of COMEN1AO) on the menu screen, so that the value the system will act upon is visibly confirmed to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Entered Option Number Back on Menu Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After normalizing the user's entered option number, the system echoes the cleaned option value back to the menu screen output field, so the user can see exactly what option value the system has recorded and will process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the menu option processing workflow to validate and act on the option number entered by the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enter Key Routes User to Menu Option Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key on the menu screen, the system proceeds to validate and process the menu option entered by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) in the navigation target field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), preparing to transfer the user back to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Key Sets Sign-On Screen as Navigation Destination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the menu screen, the system designates the Sign-On screen program (COSGN00C) as the target destination before initiating the transfer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user pressed PF3 on the menu screen and the destination program has been set to 'COSGN00C', OR the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is empty or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the return-to-sign-on navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the destination program field is empty or contains only spaces, the system defaults it to 'COSGN00C'; the system then transfers full control to the Sign-On screen program (COSGN00C), ending the current menu session

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Key Transfers User Back to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Sign-On screen is set as the destination, the system transfers control to the Sign-On program. If no destination program was explicitly set, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen program (COSGN00C) before transferring.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is neither the Enter key nor the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y' to signal that an invalid key was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unrecognized Key Sets Invalid Key Error Flag
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3, the system activates the error flag to indicate an invalid key press has occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed an unrecognized key on the menu screen and the error flag has been set to 'Y'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the error response for an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE) to inform the user that the key pressed is not recognized

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unrecognized Key Loads Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unrecognized key is pressed, the system loads the standard invalid key error message into the message area to be displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error flag is set to 'Y' and the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) has been loaded into the message field (WS-MESSAGE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the menu screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system refreshes the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name; populates all available menu options (up to 12, formatted as '[number]. [option name]'); displays the invalid key error message in the error message area (ERRMSGO) of the menu screen; and the user is required to press either the Enter key or PF3 to proceed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Screen Redisplayed with Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unrecognized key press is detected and the error message is loaded, the system redisplays the menu screen showing the invalid key error message, requiring the user to press a valid key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the main menu screen and has entered a value in the option input field (OPTIONI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key to submit their menu selection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system scans the entered option from right to left to remove trailing spaces, extracts the meaningful portion of the input, replaces any remaining spaces within the value with zeros to normalize it, stores the cleaned value as the working option (WS-OPTION), and displays the normalized option value back in the option output field (OPTIONO) on the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Normalize Menu Option Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses the Enter key on the menu screen, the system captures the option number entered, trims any trailing spaces from the right, and replaces any remaining internal spaces with zeros to produce a clean, normalized option value that is reflected back on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key, and the input has been captured and normalized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the normalized option value (WS-OPTION) contains only numeric digits
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the option value is NOT numeric, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Option Must Be a Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu option entered by the user must be a numeric value. If the user enters any non-numeric characters, the system rejects the input, sets the error flag, displays an error message, and redisplays the menu screen for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a numeric value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the normalized numeric option value (WS-OPTION) equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the option value equals zero (ZEROS), the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Option Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Even if the entered menu option is numeric, a value of zero is not a valid selection. The system must reject a zero value, set the error flag, display an error message, and redisplay the menu screen for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a numeric, non-zero value in the menu option input field and pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the normalized option value (WS-OPTION) against the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the option value is greater than the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', populates the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) with the error text 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the menu screen so the user can correct their input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Option Must Be Within the Available Range of Options
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu option entered by the user must not exceed the total number of menu options currently available. If the user enters a number greater than the maximum available options, the system rejects the input, sets the error flag, displays an error message, and redisplays the menu screen for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the menu screen and the system has captured and normalized the option input value (WS-OPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The option value (WS-OPTION) fails any one of the following conditions: (1) it is NOT numeric, OR (2) it exceeds the total count of available menu options (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT), OR (3) it equals zero (ZEROS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', moves the error message 'Please enter a valid option number...' into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), and performs the SEND-MENU-SCREEN routine to redisplay the menu screen with the error message visible, allowing the user to correct and resubmit their option selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Validation Error and Redisplay Menu for Invalid Option Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any of the menu option validations fail — the option is not numeric, equals zero, or exceeds the valid range — the system consolidates all three conditions into a single validation block, sets the error indicator, displays a unified error message, and refreshes the menu screen to allow the user to re-enter a valid option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application and has navigated to the Main Menu screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the logged-in user type is 'Regular User' (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE) AND the selected menu option's user-type designation is 'A' (Admin Only) as stored in CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the chosen option number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as an unauthorized access attempt and proceeds to deny access by activating the error flag (ERR-FLG-ON set to TRUE), clearing any prior message, populating the error message 'No access - Admin Only option...', and redisplaying the menu screen with the error message — the user remains on the menu screen and no navigation to the selected option occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Regular User Attempting Admin-Only Menu Option
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the logged-in user is a Regular User AND the selected menu option is designated as Administrator-Only access. Both conditions must be true simultaneously to trigger an access denial.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application and has navigated to the Main Menu screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the logged-in user type is NOT a Regular User (i.e., the user is an Administrator, meaning CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not apply any Admin-Only restriction check regardless of the selected option's access designation, and proceeds directly to process and navigate to the selected menu option without displaying any access denial message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Grant Unrestricted Menu Access to Administrator Users
all_rules.Rule_Description: Administrator users are not subject to the Admin-Only access restriction check. When the logged-in user is an Administrator, the system bypasses the access denial logic entirely and proceeds to process the selected menu option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is logged into the CardDemo application as a Regular User (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE) and has navigated to the Main Menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a menu option number and presses ENTER, and the system evaluates that the selected menu option's user-type designation (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the chosen option) is NOT equal to 'A' (i.e., the option is not Admin-Only)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not apply any access restriction, no error flag is set, no access denial message is displayed, and the system proceeds to process and navigate to the selected menu option

all_rules.Rule_Name: Grant Access When Selected Option Is Open to All Users
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Regular User selects a menu option that is not restricted to Administrators only (i.e., the option is open to all user types), the system grants access and proceeds to process the selected option without any access denial.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the logged-in user is a Regular User AND the selected menu option is designated as Admin-Only
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The access control check confirms both conditions are simultaneously true (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is TRUE AND CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE for the selected option equals 'A')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON (ERR-FLG-ON set to TRUE), which blocks all subsequent option processing logic from executing, ensuring the user cannot be transferred to the restricted program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Access Denied Error State for Unauthorized Menu Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Regular User attempts to access an Admin-Only menu option, the system activates the error state flag to signal that an access violation has occurred, preventing any further processing of the selected option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed that the logged-in user is a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option, and the error flag has been set to ON
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The access denial processing is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system first clears the message area (WS-MESSAGE is set to SPACES) and then populates it with the exact message: 'No access - Admin Only option...' to be displayed to the user on the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Access Denied Error Message for Admin-Only Option
all_rules.Rule_Description: When access is denied due to a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option, the system clears any prior message and populates a specific access denial message to inform the user of the restriction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to ON and populated the error message 'No access - Admin Only option...' due to a Regular User attempting to access an Admin-Only menu option
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SEND-MENU-SCREEN process is invoked, which populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name, builds all available menu options (up to 12) formatted as '[number]. [option name]', and moves the error message to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Main Menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) is refreshed and redisplayed to the user with the access denial message 'No access - Admin Only option...' visible in the error message area, the user remains on the menu screen, and no transfer to any other program occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Menu Screen After Access Denial
all_rules.Rule_Description: After denying access to an Admin-Only option for a Regular User, the system redisplays the Main Menu screen with the access denial error message, keeping the user on the menu so they can select a permitted option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a menu option on the Main Menu screen and the option has been validated as a valid numeric option within range with no access restriction errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected menu option is exactly 'COPAUS0C'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must perform a program availability check on COPAUS0C before any navigation is attempted, distinguishing this option from standard menu options that navigate directly without a prior availability check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify COPAUS0C as a Special Program Requiring Availability Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to the COPAUS0C program, the system must treat it differently from other menu options by first verifying its availability before allowing navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C' and no validation or authorization errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs an inquiry on the program 'COPAUS0C' to determine its installation status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the response of the inquiry: if the response indicates the program is available (normal response), the system proceeds with navigation; if the response indicates the program is not available (any non-normal response), the system blocks navigation and triggers an error notification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify COPAUS0C Program is Installed and Available Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring the user to the COPAUS0C program, the system must confirm that the program is physically installed and available in the application environment to prevent navigation failures.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the menu option mapped to 'COPAUS0C' and the program availability inquiry has returned a normal (successful) response confirming the program is installed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) record the current transaction ID into the session field 'From Transaction ID', (2) record the current program name into the session field 'From Program', (3) reset the program context value to zero, and (4) pass the full session communication area to the target program COPAUS0C

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pass Session Context Information When Navigating to COPAUS0C
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the COPAUS0C program is confirmed as installed, the system must record the originating transaction and program details in the session context before transferring control, ensuring the destination program knows the navigation origin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The session context fields (From Transaction ID, From Program, Program Context) have been populated and the COPAUS0C program has been confirmed as installed and available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control to program COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers complete control to the COPAUS0C program, passing the full session communication area, and the menu program relinquishes control — the user is now operating within the COPAUS0C program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate User to COPAUS0C Program When Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once session context is set and COPAUS0C is confirmed as installed, the system transfers full control to the COPAUS0C program, ending the current menu session and handing off to the target program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the menu option mapped to 'COPAUS0C' and the program availability inquiry has returned a non-normal response indicating the program is not installed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that COPAUS0C is not available in the environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) clear the current message area, (2) set the error message display color to RED, and (3) construct and display the message: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (trimmed at double-space boundary), so the user clearly understands the selected feature is unavailable

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Red Error Message When COPAUS0C Program is Not Installed
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the COPAUS0C program is found to be unavailable or not installed, the system must inform the user with a clearly visible red-colored error message that includes the specific option name, preventing any navigation attempt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the COPAUS0C program is not installed and has constructed the red error message 'This option [option name] is not installed...'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the error message construction and no navigation has occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must redisplay the full menu screen including: (1) refreshed header with current date, time, transaction ID and program name, (2) all available menu options formatted as '[number]. [option name]', and (3) the red error message visible in the error message area — allowing the user to select a different menu option

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Menu Screen After Program Not Installed Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the 'not installed' error message, the system must refresh and redisplay the full menu screen so the user can review the error and select a different valid option without losing their session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a menu option and the system is evaluating which program to invoke
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected menu option begins with the characters 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters of the program name equal 'DUMMY')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies the selected option as a placeholder 'coming soon' feature and does NOT transfer control to any program; instead it proceeds to display a coming soon notification to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Coming Soon Menu Option
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determine whether the selected menu option is mapped to a placeholder program, indicating the feature is not yet available for use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has identified that the selected menu option maps to a DUMMY placeholder program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to build the coming soon notification message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the message area (sets it to spaces/blank) so that no residual or prior message text remains before the new coming soon message is constructed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Existing Message Before Coming Soon Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before building and displaying the coming soon notification, any previously displayed message in the message area must be cleared to ensure a clean, accurate message is shown to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has identified that the selected menu option maps to a DUMMY placeholder program and the message area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to display the coming soon notification on the menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message display color attribute to GREEN, so the coming soon message is rendered in green on the screen, distinguishing it from error messages which appear in red

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Coming Soon Message Display Color to Green
all_rules.Rule_Description: Coming soon notifications must be visually distinguished from error messages by displaying them in green color, signaling to the user that this is an informational notice rather than an error or warning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has identified the selected option as a DUMMY placeholder, cleared the message area, and set the display color to green
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the coming soon notification message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs the message by concatenating: the literal text 'This option ', followed by the name of the selected menu option (trimmed at the first space), followed by the literal text 'is coming soon ...', and stores this combined text into the message field to be displayed on the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Coming Soon Message with Option Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: The coming soon notification message must be dynamically constructed by combining the literal text 'This option', the name of the selected menu option, and the phrase 'is coming soon ...' to provide a clear, context-specific message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The coming soon message has been built and the message color has been set to green
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes processing for a DUMMY placeholder menu option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system refreshes and sends the menu screen to the user with the header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name), all available menu options displayed, and the green coming soon message shown in the error message area — the user remains on the menu screen and is not transferred to any other program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Menu Screen with Coming Soon Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: After building the coming soon notification, the system must redisplay the menu screen with the green coming soon message visible to the user, keeping the user on the menu so they can select a different available option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid menu option number and access has been granted (option is numeric, within range, not zero, and not an Admin-Only option for a regular user)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the program name mapped to the selected menu option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the program name is exactly 'COPAUS0C', the system follows the special availability-check path; if the first 5 characters of the program name are 'DUMMY', the system follows the coming-soon placeholder path; for all other program names, the system follows the standard program transfer path

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Program Navigation Path Based on Selected Menu Option
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a valid menu option with granted access, the system determines the appropriate navigation path by evaluating the program name associated with the selected option — routing to a special availability-checked program, a placeholder, or a standard program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is 'COPAUS0C'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the program 'COPAUS0C' is installed and available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the program is available, the system proceeds to record origin details and transfer control to COPAUS0C; if the program is not available, the system displays an error message and returns the user to the menu for correction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify Availability of COPAUS0C Program Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system verifies that the program is currently installed and available in the environment to prevent navigation to a non-existent program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C' and the program has been confirmed as available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the origin transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Origin Transaction ID Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system records the current transaction identifier as the originating transaction so the target program can identify where the navigation originated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C', the program is confirmed available, and the origin transaction ID has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the origin program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Origin Program Name Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system records the current program name as the originating program so the target program can identify the source of navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C', the program is confirmed available, and both origin transaction ID and origin program name have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes preparation to transfer control to COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is set to zero (ZEROS) in the session communication area, indicating a fresh entry into the target program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context Before Transferring to COPAUS0C
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the COPAUS0C program, the system resets the program context indicator to zero, signaling to the target program that it is being entered fresh from the menu rather than from a mid-flow return.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program 'COPAUS0C' is confirmed available, and the session communication area has been updated with the origin transaction ID, origin program name, and a reset program context of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the program 'COPAUS0C' and the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the target program; the target program receives control with complete session information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to COPAUS0C Program with Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming availability and recording origin details, the system transfers full control to the COPAUS0C program, passing the complete session communication area so the target program has all necessary context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to program 'COPAUS0C'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the program 'COPAUS0C' is not installed or not available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the error message color to RED, and displays the message: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option, delimited by two spaces); the user is returned to the menu screen for correction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Program Not Available Error When COPAUS0C Is Not Installed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user selects the menu option associated with COPAUS0C but the program is not installed in the environment, the system informs the user with a clearly highlighted error message and returns them to the menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name begins with 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters equal 'DUMMY')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the program type for the selected option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the message color to GREEN, and displays the message: 'This option [option name] is coming soon ...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option, delimited by a single space); the user remains on the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Coming Soon Message for Placeholder Menu Options
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder program (not yet implemented), the system informs the user that the feature is planned but not yet available, without navigating away from the menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is not 'COPAUS0C' and does not begin with 'DUMMY'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the selected standard program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the origin transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Origin Transaction ID Before Transferring to Standard Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any standard (non-COPAUS0C, non-DUMMY) program, the system records the current transaction identifier as the originating transaction so the target program can identify the navigation source.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is not 'COPAUS0C' and does not begin with 'DUMMY', and the origin transaction ID has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the selected standard program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the origin program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area before the transfer occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Origin Program Name Before Transferring to Standard Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any standard program, the system records the current program name as the originating program so the target program can identify the source of navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option whose associated program name is not 'COPAUS0C' and does not begin with 'DUMMY', and both origin transaction ID and origin program name have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes preparation to transfer control to the selected standard program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is set to zero (ZEROS) in the session communication area, indicating a fresh entry into the target program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context Before Transferring to Standard Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any standard program, the system resets the program context indicator to zero, signaling to the target program that it is being entered fresh from the menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid menu option mapped to a standard program (not 'COPAUS0C' and not beginning with 'DUMMY'), and the session communication area has been updated with the origin transaction ID, origin program name, and a reset program context of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the program identified by CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME for the selected option, and the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the target program; the target program receives control with complete session information including origin transaction ID, origin program name, and program context set to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Selected Standard Program with Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording origin details and resetting program context, the system transfers full control to the user's selected standard program, passing the complete session communication area so the target program has all necessary context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the main menu screen and no active session context exists (communication area length is zero, indicating no prior session has been established)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the absence of an active session upon screen entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the originating program reference to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On program) and immediately redirects the user to the Sign-On screen, preventing any access to the menu without authentication

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to access the main menu without an active session, the system must redirect them to the Sign-On screen to authenticate before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authenticated user is on the main menu screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 function key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and initiates the return-to-sign-on process, transferring the user back to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Sign-On Screen When User Presses PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authenticated user on the main menu screen explicitly presses PF3, the system treats this as a deliberate request to go back or log out, and routes the user back to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The return-to-sign-on process has been triggered either due to no active session or PF3 key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the destination program field and finds it contains LOW-VALUES (uninitialized) or SPACES (blank — not explicitly set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system automatically sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) as the default, ensuring no transfer occurs to an undefined or blank destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen When Not Explicitly Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring the user to the Sign-On screen, the system verifies that a destination program has been explicitly set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults it to the Sign-On program to ensure the user always lands on a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to 'COSGN00C' (either explicitly via PF3 or defaulted due to no session or unset destination)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Full control is transferred to the Sign-On program ('COSGN00C'), the current menu program terminates, and the user is presented with the Sign-On screen to authenticate or re-authenticate. No communication area is passed, ensuring a clean session start

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer User Control to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the destination has been confirmed or defaulted to the Sign-On screen, the system transfers full control to the Sign-On program, ending the current menu session and presenting the user with the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header population process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins preparing the header information for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it internally as the source data for all subsequent date and time formatting operations on the menu screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the menu screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time so that accurate and up-to-date contextual information can be displayed to the user on every screen refresh.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header population process is in progress and application title constants (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02) are defined in the application communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the menu screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 (TITLE01O) on the menu screen is set to the value of application constant CCDA-TITLE01, and Application Title Line 2 (TITLE02O) on the menu screen is set to the value of application constant CCDA-TITLE02

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Application Title Lines on Menu Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu screen header must display two lines of application title text sourced from predefined application-level constants (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02), ensuring consistent branding and identification across all menu screen presentations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header population process is in progress and the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is available in the working session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the menu screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID field (TRNNAMEO) on the menu screen header is set to the current transaction identifier value from WS-TRANID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Transaction ID on Menu Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu screen header must display the current active transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) so that users and support staff can identify which transaction is currently running.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu screen header population process is in progress and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is available in the working session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the menu screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Program Name field (PGMNAMEO) on the menu screen header is set to the current program name value from WS-PGMNAME

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Program Name on Menu Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The menu screen header must display the name of the currently executing program (WS-PGMNAME) to provide users and support staff with clear identification of the active program context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA, containing separate components for month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH), day (WS-CURDATE-DAY), and year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the date for display on the menu screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is placed into the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is placed into the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), only the last two digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) are placed into the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), and the fully assembled MM/DD/YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is set into the Date field (CURDATEO) on the menu screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date as MM/DD/YY on Menu Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date retrieved from the system must be formatted into MM/DD/YY format before being displayed on the menu screen header. The month and day are taken directly from the system date, while only the last two digits of the year are used.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored as part of WS-CURDATE-DATA, containing separate components for hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS), minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE), and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the time for display on the menu screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is placed into the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is placed into the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is placed into the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), and the fully assembled HH:MM:SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is set into the Time field (CURTIMEO) on the menu screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time as HH:MM:SS on Menu Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time retrieved from the system must be formatted into HH:MM:SS format before being displayed on the menu screen header, using hours, minutes, and seconds components from the system time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen with an active session, and the menu screen has been previously displayed awaiting user input

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message field (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces, the error message color attribute (ERRMSGC of COMEN1AO) is set to RED (DFHRED), and a message is constructed and loaded into WS-MESSAGE in the format: 'This option [option name] is not installed...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option), delimited at double-space; the menu screen is then redisplayed with this red error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unavailable Program Error Notification
