Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the main menu screen, has entered a valid option number with no prior errors, and the selected option is not mapped to program COPAUS0C
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first 5 characters of the program name associated with the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME for the selected option) equal 'DUMMY'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message field (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces, the error message color attribute (ERRMSGC of COMEN1AO) is set to GREEN (DFHGREEN), and a message is constructed and loaded into WS-MESSAGE in the format: 'This option [option name] is coming soon...' where [option name] is the name of the selected menu option (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME for the selected option), delimited at first space; the menu screen is then redisplayed with this green informational message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Coming Soon Feature Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a menu option that is mapped to a placeholder program (not yet implemented), the system informs the user that the feature is planned but not yet available, displaying the message in green color.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected, an appropriate message has been loaded into the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE), and the system is preparing to redisplay the menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The send menu screen process is initiated (SEND-MENU-SCREEN is performed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) is moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO), making the message available for display to the user on the menu screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Transfer to Screen Display Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redisplaying the menu screen, any error or informational message that has been loaded into the working storage message field is transferred to the corresponding screen output field so it becomes visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected, the appropriate error message has been moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO of COMEN1AO), the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID and program name, and all available menu options (up to 12) have been formatted and placed in their respective screen option fields (OPTN001O through OPTN012O)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The menu screen send operation is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete menu screen (map COMEN1A from mapset COMEN01) is sent to the user's terminal using the populated output map (COMEN1AO) with the ERASE option, displaying the refreshed menu with all options and the error message visible, so the user can review the error and re-enter their selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Menu Screen Redisplay After Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After any error condition is detected and the error message is prepared, the menu screen is refreshed and sent back to the user with updated header information, all menu options, and the error message displayed, allowing the user to review and correct their input.

description:
COMEN01C is the Main Menu program for regular users in the CardDemo application. It displays a navigable menu screen, validates the user's menu selection, enforces access control by restricting admin-only options from regular users, and transfers control to the appropriate sub-program based on the user's choice. If no valid session exists, the user is redirected to the sign-on screen.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: None - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Session Validation - Check if a valid user session exists when the menu program starts. If no session data is present, redirect the user to the Sign-On screen to authenticate before accessing the menu. 2: Initial Menu Display - On the first visit to the main menu, initialize the screen and display the menu to the user with all available options populated and header information shown. 3: Menu Screen Input Capture - Capture the user's input from the main menu screen, including the option number they have entered. 4: Navigation Key Handling - Detect which key the user pressed (Enter, PF3, or other). If PF3 is pressed, return the user to the Sign-On screen. If an unrecognized key is pressed, display an invalid key error message and redisplay the menu. 5: Menu Option Input Validation - Validate the option number entered by the user. Ensure it is numeric, not zero, and within the valid range of available menu options. If invalid, display an error message prompting the user to enter a valid option number. 6: User Access Control Check - Verify that the logged-in user has permission to access the selected menu option. If the option is restricted to Administrators only and the current user is a Regular user, deny access and display a 'No access - Admin Only option' message. 7: Program Availability Check - For specific menu options (e.g., COPAUS0C), verify that the target program is installed and available in the system before attempting to navigate to it. If the program is not installed, display an error message indicating the option is not available. 8: Coming Soon Option Handling - If the selected menu option maps to a placeholder (DUMMY) program, display a 'coming soon' message to the user in green, indicating the feature is not yet available. 9: Menu Option Navigation - Transfer control to the appropriate program corresponding to the user's valid menu selection, passing along the session communication area so the target program knows the origin. 10: Return to Sign-On - Transfer the user back to the Sign-On screen, either when no session exists or when the user explicitly presses PF3 to log out or go back. 11: Header Information Population - Populate the menu screen header with application title, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time to provide context to the user. 12: Menu Options Display Build - Dynamically build and display up to 12 menu option entries on the screen by combining each option's number and name into a formatted text line for each available menu item. 13: Error Message Display - Display appropriate error messages on the menu screen when validation fails, access is denied, a program is unavailable, or an invalid key is pressed, and redisplay the menu for the user to correct their input.
